features.name: hedge_term_rate
features.definition: Across all counter-argument comments, how many hedging words (might, could, perhaps) occur per 100 words?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads (malformed/missing -> null). Empty list -> 0. Lowercase all comments; tokenise words with re.findall(r"[a-z']+", text). hedges = number of tokens equal to 'might', 'could' or 'perhaps' across all comments; total = total tokens across all comments. Return 100*hedges/total; if total==0 return null. Purely literal matching, no semantic filtering.

h0: hedge_term_rate has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher hedge_term_rate in counter-arguments is associated with a higher probability of the OP changing their view.
note: "Persuasive" operationalised as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); association only, not causal. Hedging is operationalised only by the literal listed words might/could/perhaps (the hypothesis's examples); other hedges (maybe, possibly, seems) are not counted, and 'could' may be non-hedging (e.g. quoted or in questions). Comments are pooled by row; no per-comment outcome is available so comment-level persuasiveness cannot be tested. Comment text may include post-outcome content; timing is unknown. Fit with a linear probability model (OLS).
